final_recommendation: The room converged on a forced merger of Credit Suisse with UBS over the weekend, structured with substantial government loss protection (CHF 5-10bn backstop), SNB liquidity facility (CHF 100bn+), emergency ordinance bypassing normal approval processes, and closure before Asian markets open Monday. AT1 bondholders and equity to be written to zero.
key_conflicts: FINMA vs AT1 holders: whether to write down AT1 to validate Basel III framework vs legal/market risk to AT1 asset class
UBS vs Federal Council: UBS demands maximum loss protection vs government wants to minimize fiscal cost
AT1 bondholders vs equity holders: fight over loss absorption hierarchy and who gets wiped out first
FINMA vs Federal Council: regulator wants legally correct process vs politicians prioritize speed and certainty
key_concessions: Federal Council will provide CHF 5-10bn loss-sharing guarantee and emergency ordinance bypassing democratic process
SNB will provide CHF 100-200bn liquidity facility accepting collateral risk despite preference to avoid solvency support
UBS will agree to acquire CS and accept integration risk in exchange for massive government protection and near-zero purchase price
FINMA will accept emergency ordinance bypassing normal process and provide regulatory capital forbearance
CS management/board will accept forced sale at nominal price, resignations, and compensation clawbacks
red_lines: Transaction must close before Asian markets open Monday morning - time constraint is absolute
UBS walk-away threshold: will refuse if government won't backstop at least CHF 5-10bn of losses
AT1 treatment must either wipe equity first or convert AT1 to equity to preserve creditor hierarchy
SNB will provide liquidity but demands government fiscal backstop for credit losses - will not take solvency risk alone
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Post-closing UBS integration execution risk dismissed as 'not a weekend problem'
20-30% wealth client flight accepted as inevitable even with successful announcement
Cross-border coordination with Fed/ECB/BoE treated as manageable via existing regulator contacts rather than as potential blocking issue
Political sustainability and parliamentary backlash noted but deprioritized relative to immediate systemic risk
downstream_risk_variables: Actual UBS due diligence findings on CS asset quality during Saturday review
Scale of weekend client redemption instructions submitted via private bankers
AT1 bondholder litigation strategy and speed of injunction attempts
Foreign regulator (Fed, ECB, BoE) acceptance of emergency merger structure
Market contagion to other European banks on Monday despite CS resolution
UBS share price reaction and credit rating impact
Actual loss realization on government-backstopped CS portfolios
uncertainty_notes: Critical uncertainties remaining: (1) whether UBS will accept terms even with CHF 5-10bn backstop or will demand more; (2) exact AT1 treatment mechanism (write-down vs conversion) and resulting litigation risk; (3) scale of weekend client flight before announcement; (4) whether Sunday 18:00 announcement deadline is achievable given negotiation complexity; (5) foreign regulator coordination success; (6) whether 20-30% accepted client flight is realistic or optimistic.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: Opening rationale states 'statements alone cannot reverse' confidence collapse and 'Pure liquidation is systemically unacceptable' - drove the entire merger recommendation rather than liquidity-only approach
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS acquisition is the explicit 'BASE CASE: Forced merger with UBS' and the entire decision sequence is structured around UBS negotiations - this IS the recommended solution
marker_evidence.government_support: Government loss protection (CHF 5-10bn backstop) and SNB liquidity facility (CHF 100bn+) are mandatory 'Package elements (all required)' and UBS walk-away threshold explicitly depends on it
marker_evidence.client_flight: Identified as 'D2. Weekend client/counterparty panic' with 60-70% probability of acceleration, drives Sunday 18:00 announcement deadline, and shapes explicit deposit protection messaging requirements
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 write-down is package element #4 labeled 'MOST CONTENTIOUS', with three options analyzed and recommendation to write down to zero - directly shapes capital structure decision
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: Entire section on 'AT1 bondholders vs equity holders: fight over loss absorption hierarchy' and FINMA's dilemma between validating Basel III vs destroying AT1 market - forces choice between Option A/B/C
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 legal challenges scored as 'D3' risk with 25-30% probability and 'expect immediate injunctions', but mitigation is to 'move fast enough that injunctions come after closing' - acknowledged but not blocking
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Time constraint described as 'absolute' with detailed hour-by-hour decision sequence Friday 23:00 through Sunday 18:00, and 'every hour of weekend uncertainty accelerates Monday flight risk' - drives entire timeline
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Monday 09:00 Asian open is the hard deadline throughout, with detailed 'FAIL POINTS' scenario showing CS stock free fall, client flight, and contagion if no announcement - this constraint structures the entire weekend plan
